answer:
Headline results of agent run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (stride 20, read-only report):

RECORDS AND ANOMALIES
- Records analysed: 759 (stride 20; 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z, 3.314% of the time window)
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 above the catalogue completeness magnitude Mc)
- Pumping: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days (net extraction)
- LBNL/NCEDC (GDR 859) March 2016 catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07

CALIBRATED (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — this is the calibrated probability):
- b = 1.0:  Sigma = -5.449, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.0001198, P(Mw>=5.5) over the observed volume = 5.236e-06, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.03719
- b = 0.73: Sigma = -5.319, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.004922,  P(Mw>=5.5) over the observed volume = 0.0002155, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.2809
- b = 0.65: Sigma = -5.281, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.01474,   P(Mw>=5.5) over the observed volume = 0.0006484, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.4653

UPPER BOUND (DAS-based, uncalibrated magnitudes; every DAS detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts — this is the upper bound, not calibrated):
- b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated LBNL-catalogue estimate gives P(Mw>=5.5) of at most ~1.5% per year (b=0.65 scenario), i.e. a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 earthquake is unlikely; the DAS-based Sigma of -2.698 and P(Mw>=5.5)/yr of 0.078 is an upper bound only, because DAS magnitudes are uncalibrated and counting every detection above Mc over-counts events.
